context: Tests whether the agent identifies a RHEL UBI major bump as license-aware AND leads its recommended action with a family-escape (Fedora / Rocky / Alma / distroless / Wolfi) rather than the legalistic 'get sign-off and bump within UBI' path. The license-aware classification alone isn't enough — the advice must steer toward escaping the licensed family by default, with in-family + sign-off retained only as a secondary path for users with hard constraints.

checklist.name: Classification is license-aware
checklist.description: advice.md classifies the bump as license-aware. Critical: not safe-mechanical (which would be wrong because the rubric's precedence has license-aware > safe-mechanical when both apply).

checklist.name: Cites 'RHEL UBI major bump' indicator
checklist.description: Indicators section names 'RHEL UBI major bump' (verbatim or clearly equivalent) and explains that base subscription entitlements differ across UBI majors.

checklist.name: Notes the JVM workload would otherwise be safe-mechanical
checklist.description: The advice acknowledges (in Notes or in the indicator discussion) that the JVM workload pattern itself is otherwise safe-mechanical (Eclipse Temurin re-resolves system libs), but the licensing precedence takes precedence.

checklist.name: Recommended action leads with family-escape
checklist.description: Recommended action recommends a license-free alternative as the primary path — Fedora, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, distroless-java, or Wolfi/Chainguard. NOT 'apply mechanically' and NOT just 'flag for sign-off and bump to ubi9'. Sign-off + in-family bump is acceptable as a secondary path in Notes (e.g. for users with hard constraints like an existing OpenShift subscription), but the default recommendation must escape the licensed family.

checklist.name: No fabricated CVE references
checklist.description: The advice does NOT cite specific CVE identifiers.
